analysis:
Examined all supplied patches, source and mode metadata. ci-master.yml:65,73 makes provider/cluster PR testing label-only; pushes retain testing. Lines 35–38 isolate unrelated label events but let new revisions supersede opted-in runs. The new label-removal job (41–57) has write permissions but checks out no PR code, uses quoted environment values and exposes no token in its commands. Release Integrity and Docs Lint remain automatic, with pinned actions, push-only cache saves and existing cached-git validation unchanged.

claude.yml:20–21 and codex.yml:25–26,111–112 move jobs to ubuntu-24.04 and bound runtime. Their existing event admission, action pins, secret use, permissions and feedback handling are unchanged; no evidence establishes a runner-specific security control lost by this move. Existing agent-input risks are not new findings.

The darkbloom-route.yml patch adds validated 1–9 attempt limits (85–88), HTTPS-only five-second requests, bounded retry sleeps and elapsed-time admission (181–241), sanitized configuration diagnostics and allowlisted failure diagnostics. Numeric Retry-After cannot inject shell commands; temporary response files are cleaned up. No supported new disclosure or authorization bypass was identified.

These workflow changes do not directly modify provider encryption, cache isolation (T-041), grants (T-052/T-053), qualification (T-054/A-017), privileged helpers or billing. They do reduce automatic pre-merge native regression coverage. Integration must examine provider-plan.yml, provider-tests.yml and ci-tested-tree.py together: run_tests=false must not create reusable evidence that native tests passed, and deduplication must require the appropriate completed lanes, including cluster_gpu. Those implementations and merge-policy details are absent here, so this remains a material unverified contract rather than a finding. The routing patch also omits surrounding response validation/fallback source; reconcile it with other supplied passes before concluding on routing behavior.
